one_line: Rights-bound campaign preparation with evidence-stale authority revocation.
what_it_does: Lets an agent inspect rights, prepare an exact campaign manifest, obtain human approval, and publish only through a capability bound to current evidence.
leverage_rationale: WebMCP is the core mechanism for exposing a precise, parameterless publish capability only after human approval and withdrawing it when evidence changes; generic UI driving cannot reproduce this boundary as reliably.
leverage_evidence: Frames show 3/3 current changing to 2/3 current and publish authority removed.
Agent discovers structured tools, inspects rights, and prepares a versioned manifest.
Transcript states the one-shot publish tool is bound to the approved manifest and disappears when stale.
execution_rationale: The packet presents a highly coherent end-to-end workflow: inspect, select, manifest, human approval, rights update, repair, reapproval, and receipt/audit. Visual frames corroborate the key states, though live execution is claimed rather than independently observed.
execution_evidence: Three frame sheets show tool discovery, eligible assets, manifest review, invalidation, and reapproval states.
Devpost packaging visibly highlights 3/3 to 2/3 and authority removal.
Transcript describes matching publish receipt and audit record.
impact_rationale: Creative-operations teams have a concrete consequential problem: agents need to prepare campaigns without receiving stale or overbroad publishing authority. The evidence-bound workflow directly addresses that risk.
impact_evidence: Specific Japan/Instagram/TikTok campaign scenario with commercial rights and dates.
Human-only approval and stale-proof withdrawal are visible product behaviors.
Audit and receipt matching are part of the demonstrated workflow.
creativity_rationale: The concept turns WebMCP capability exposure into revocable, evidence-bound authority rather than merely a tool list, with a memorable stale-approval lifecycle.
creativity_evidence: Explicit distinction between preparation, approval, and one-shot publication.
Rights update invalidates the old approval and forces a new manifest.
Capability surface visibly changes with evidence freshness.
usability_note: Clear dark operations UI, manifest review, current-proof counters, and explicit human controls; some dense text is small.
standouts: Strongest evidence-bound authority model in the packet.
advance_reason: Exceptional leverage and unusually complete evidence of a consequential, human-gated workflow.

one_line: Privacy-preserving benefits screening across agencies using predicate answers instead of records.
what_it_does: Lets a caseworker screen one household for six benefit programs by querying four data origins for yes/no predicates while keeping underlying records at each origin.
leverage_rationale: Origin-scoped WebMCP tools expose predicates without exposing records, and consent withdrawal removes registrations rather than returning ordinary refusals. A general UI agent cannot comparably enforce this data boundary.
leverage_evidence: Transcript states 11 questions, 10 answered, zero record fields disclosed.
Frames visibly show Vouchsafe dashboard/detail workflow, though tool calls are not legible.
Consent withdrawal is described as aborting tool registration and making programs indeterminate.
execution_rationale: The packet coherently demonstrates a populated Vouchsafe workbench and privacy-oriented flow, with transcript-level end-to-end claims. Visual frames show product surfaces and populated metrics but not a fully readable final case outcome.
execution_evidence: Frame sheets show landing, dashboard, detail, and populated states.
Transcript gives concrete four-origin, six-program results and disclosure ledger behavior.
Devpost video packaging clearly presents the product and scenario.
impact_rationale: Benefits caseworkers and households facing legally siloed records; the solution addresses a high-friction, high-consequence access problem while preserving privacy.
impact_evidence: Specific heating, food, and childcare benefit screening use case.
No income, address, or roster is returned; only predicates and audit references.
Indeterminate outcomes after consent withdrawal preserve honest uncertainty.
creativity_rationale: Using origin-scoped capabilities and predicate attestations to solve inter-agency legal data separation is a novel interaction model with substantial ambition.
creativity_evidence: Four independent origins and no central record pooling.
Consent modeled as exposure to a named origin.
Disclosure ledger shows what stayed and what crossed boundaries.
usability_note: The workbench and results framing are clear, though frame text is too small to inspect in detail.
red_flags: Screenshots alone do not prove encryption/storage properties, but transcript provides coherent behavioral evidence.
standouts: Honest indeterminate state after consent withdrawal.
advance_reason: High-impact, technically distinctive use of WebMCP with a credible end-to-end scenario.

one_line: Agent-native vehicle configurator, garage twin, owner guide, and 3D creation engine.
what_it_does: Provides 49 WebMCP tools across vehicle configuration, synchronized garage state, owner-guide inspection, and measurement-driven 3D creation.
leverage_rationale: Structured tools span shared vehicle state, revision-gated mutations, undo, component measurement, and multi-context coordination; an agent driving a rich 3D UI would be substantially less reliable.
leverage_evidence: About text enumerates 49 tools across five contexts.
Frames show RX2 configurator, paint selection, 3D vehicle, and developer inspection states.
Claims include human interruption, revision gates, undo, and source/measurement-basis results.
execution_rationale: The product surface is coherent and visually polished, with a working-looking configurator and multiple connected experiences. No video and limited direct agent execution evidence cap confidence.
execution_evidence: Frames show landing, experience cards, RX2 3D configurator, paint controls, pricing, and performance information.
Devpost packaging shows a 49-tool vehicle journey and a deployed product.
Public repo and live demo are reported alive.
impact_rationale: Car shoppers, owners, and creators can plausibly benefit from shared configuration and an agent-operable owner experience, though the fictional vehicle limits immediate practical reach.
impact_evidence: Clear vehicle configurator, garage, owner-guide, and creation-engine audiences.
Shared 3D twin and measured components support meaningful owner and builder workflows.
creativity_rationale: The breadth of a single agent-native vehicle journey combining commerce configuration, ownership knowledge, synchronized 3D state, and creation is ambitious and memorable.
creativity_evidence: Three connected experiences around one vehicle.
Measurement-driven 3D Creation Engine and named components.
Human-agent shared state across multiple page contexts.
usability_note: Strong visual hierarchy and approachable configurator; the breadth may increase complexity.
red_flags: No submitted video; frame sheets show mostly static UI and no legible tool invocation.
advance_reason: High ambition and substantial structured surface, despite weaker direct agent evidence.

one_line: Deterministic website-side policy enforcement for agent purchasing actions.
what_it_does: Stores human purchasing rules, validates structured agent proposals, blocks violations, and requires confirmation before one-time execution.
leverage_rationale: WebMCP handlers become enforcement points inside the website: structured calls are checked against mission versions, trusted values, freshness, and execute-once protections rather than merely routed to UI actions.
leverage_evidence: Frames show five tools, structured order call, schema/rule/result pipeline, BLOCK, ASK HUMAN, and SAFE ACTION COMPLETED.
Transcript describes ALLOW, BLOCK, and UNDETERMINED results plus stale-action replay protection.
Rules include maximum total, quantity, delivery, and approved vendors.
execution_rationale: The central workflow is unusually well evidenced visually, including both blocked unsafe input and corrected human-confirmed completion. Minor uncertainty remains about live deployment depth.
execution_evidence: Frame sheets visibly show invalid order quantity/location/price and corrected safe action.
Devpost packaging presents a live demo and boundary-control workflow.
About text claims automated tests and public deployment.
impact_rationale: People delegating purchases to agents have a real need for enforceable spending and delivery boundaries; deterministic blocking and explanations directly reduce consequential errors.
impact_evidence: Concrete $100, quantity-1, Office A policy.
Unsafe $395/quantity-5/Warehouse B request is visibly blocked.
Human confirmation is required for the compliant action.
creativity_rationale: The fresh angle is treating the website/WebMCP boundary as the policy enforcement layer, with explicit stale and replay protections rather than relying on agent obedience.
creativity_evidence: Agent proposes, website verifies, human confirms, execute once.
IntentLock handler visibly separates schema, rule check, and result.
Supports permission-change requests and indeterminate outcomes.
usability_note: Clear rule/proposal/result progression and explicit block explanations.
advance_reason: Excellent WebMCP leverage with visually demonstrated blocking and confirmed completion.

one_line: Shared WebMCP-operable Doppler-effect laboratory for learners and agents.
what_it_does: Lets humans and agents discover, configure, run, inspect, compare, and record interactive Doppler simulations through semantic tools.
leverage_rationale: Semantic controls make a visual/audio physics instrument precisely configurable and inspectable by an agent while preserving the human-visible simulation and shared state.
leverage_evidence: About text specifies 11 tools, including discovery, state, configuration, playback, reset, and recording.
Frames show library navigation, Doppler Lab, active scene, side panel, and inspection tooling.
The simulation visibly changes as the car moves while the lab panel updates.
execution_rationale: The packet shows a coherent product from library to loaded Doppler Lab and active simulation, with a useful educational surface. Exact agent calls and final recorded artifact are not fully legible.
execution_evidence: Frames show homepage, experiments library, physics selection, simulation scene, controls, and explanatory panel.
Public repo and live demo are reported alive.
No video is submitted, limiting end-to-end certainty.
impact_rationale: Science learners and classrooms have a clear desire for inspectable, interactive experiments; sharing precise control with an agent can improve explanation and exploration.
impact_evidence: Specific Doppler effect lesson with approaching/receding vehicles and sound.
Human sees, hears, and modifies the same experiment as the agent.
Classroom/student audience is explicit.
creativity_rationale: The shared scientific-instrument framing and semantic control of physics/audio state is a fresh, ambitious application beyond generic chat tutoring.
creativity_evidence: Agent operates the same live simulation rather than hiding it behind generated text.
Links visual state, physics calculations, audio, and recorded output.
Discovery and open-simulation tools extend beyond one static demo.
usability_note: Clear experiment-library-to-lab flow; dense inspection panel may be technical for novices.
red_flags: Submission says Esbiko is an existing open-source platform; challenge extension is the new work.
No video and small frame text limit direct verification.
standouts: Strong shared human-agent scientific workspace concept.
advance_reason: Useful and creative education application with meaningful structured-agent delta.

one_line: Playable maze where an agent inspects, solves, and executes the path through WebMCP.
what_it_does: Provides generated mazes, manual controls, and WebMCP tools for an AI agent to analyze and navigate to escape.
leverage_rationale: Structured maze inspection and path execution are more reliable than pixel-level UI driving, but a capable general agent could solve the same game with moderate effort.
leverage_evidence: About text claims inspect/solve/play tools and a 20x20 maze.
Devpost description includes frames of AI analysis, execution, progress, and successful escape.
No submitted video or frame sheets were available for direct review.
execution_rationale: The written packet describes a complete generated-maze and successful-completion flow, but evidence is limited to packaging text and a Devpost screenshot with no submitted video frames.
execution_evidence: About text lists landing, generated maze, active execution, and final escape screenshots.
Live demo and public repo are reported alive.
No frame sheets and no video transcript materially limit execution confidence.
impact_rationale: Players and playful human-agent collaboration have identifiable entertainment value, though the use case is narrow and the packet does not establish deeper consequences.
impact_evidence: Clear playable game and Human + AI maze challenge framing.
Successful escape and solution details are claimed in screenshot captions.
creativity_rationale: Agent actually solving and playing a maze is a competent, engaging WebMCP application, but the core game concept is familiar.
creativity_evidence: Agent analyzes a generated maze and executes a path.
Human and AI share a playable challenge.
usability_note: Manual controls and progress panels appear straightforward, but direct usability cannot be checked without frames.
red_flags: No submitted video frame sheets; evidence is packaging/text only.
advance_reason: Plausible and complete-sounding, but thin evidence and only moderate differentiation do not justify advancing over stronger packets.

one_line: Thai voice interface for reading, filling, and submitting English web forms.
what_it_does: Turns semantically sound forms into typed WebMCP tools and lets Thai speakers use voice to read, translate, fill, correct, and explicitly confirm submission.
leverage_rationale: Typed semantic form tools and structured validation replace fragile pixel guessing, while shared feedback enables correction and confirmation; general UI driving is substantially less reliable for accessibility-critical forms.
leverage_evidence: About text specifies describe_form, read_form, fill_form, and submit_form tools.
Workflow includes typed validation feedback and self-correction rather than red-border scraping.
Explicit confirmation gates submission.
execution_rationale: The architecture and workflow are coherent, but there is no submitted video and only one gallery image; end-to-end voice behavior is claimed rather than visibly established.
execution_evidence: About text details MV3 bridge, Zod schemas, Thai speech, translation, and Web Speech API.
Live demo is reported alive.
No video transcript and limited visual evidence cap the score.
impact_rationale: Thai speakers facing English-only visa, university, or airline forms—and blind, low-vision, motor-impaired, and elderly users—have a concrete accessibility need directly addressed by the workflow.
impact_evidence: Specific Thai-to-English form use case.
Keeps names in Latin script, translates free text, matches dropdowns, and asks in Thai when uncertain.
Never submits without explicit confirmation.
creativity_rationale: Combining browser-native semantic tools with Thai voice accessibility and validation-driven self-correction is a strong, original synthesis.
creativity_evidence: One typed tool boundary serves JSON Schema and runtime validation.
Two-world extension bridge separates microphone from document.modelContext.
Targets accessibility as a capability rather than a special-needs add-on.
usability_note: Voice-first flow is thoughtfully designed; dependency on speech/translation services may affect reliability.
red_flags: No video evidence; API-key access model inferred from GPT/Paxa dependencies and may be unclear.
standouts: Strong accessibility impact and concrete bilingual workflow.
advance_reason: High-impact accessibility application with meaningful semantic-tool leverage despite limited visual evidence.

one_line: Privacy-first, explainable apparel size recommendations across brand-specific charts.
what_it_does: Compares shopper measurements and fit preferences with garment-specific charts, including pasted product links and explainable alternatives.
leverage_rationale: Structured garment/chart/recommendation tools improve precision and explainability over labels, but a general agent could likely achieve similar results with real but manageable friction.
leverage_evidence: About text lists five structured tools for garments, charts, recommendations, product links, and comparisons.
Measurements remain in-browser by default and retailer credentials are not needed.
No video or submitted frame sheets are available.
execution_rationale: The product scope is coherent and specific, but the packet supplies only written claims and Devpost packaging with no direct result frame or video.
execution_evidence: Clear input/output list: recommended size, confidence, fit details, warnings, alternative.
Live demo reported alive.
No video transcript or frame sheets limit end-to-end evidence.
impact_rationale: Online apparel shoppers have a widespread fit and returns problem; brand-specific, explainable sizing has credible direct value even for a niche retailer-independent workflow.
impact_evidence: Specific chest/waist/shoulder/sleeve mismatch problem.
Supports real product links and avoids marketplace scraping.
Privacy-first local measurement handling is a strong fit.
creativity_rationale: The privacy-preserving, retailer-independent angle is useful, but size recommendation is a familiar category and the new interaction model is modest.
creativity_evidence: Compares brand-specific charts rather than generic labels.
Explainable area-by-area fit and alternative size outputs.
usability_note: The described inputs and outputs are understandable; actual UI usability is not evidenced.
red_flags: No submitted video or frame sheets; claims cannot be visually checked.
standouts: Clear niche value and privacy posture.
advance_reason: Credible utility, but evidence is thin and WebMCP adds a moderate rather than major delta.

one_line: Agent-coordinated flight-cancellation recovery across flight, hotel, transport, budget, and notifications.
what_it_does: Exposes 12 WebMCP tools for searching and holding flights, booking hotels and transport, notifying contacts, tracking cost, and generating itineraries with human confirmation gates.
leverage_rationale: The structured, stateful multi-step tool surface lets the browser coordinate recovery across several travel domains without a custom agent; generic UI driving would be materially less reliable.
leverage_evidence: About text enumerates 12 tools across flights, hotels, ground transport, notifications, cost, and itinerary.
Devpost screenshot visibly shows ChatGPT-like browser coordination and confirmed reservation details.
Human confirmation is retained for consequential actions.
execution_rationale: The packet shows a coherent multi-step recovery product and packaging with reservation, itinerary, and budget states. No video limits direct observation but the visual product surface is substantial.
execution_evidence: Frame sheet shows repeated travel recovery application states and agent workspace.
Devpost media visibly includes confirmed reservation, trip total, and over-budget state.
Live demo and public repo are reported alive.
impact_rationale: Flight cancellation before a time-critical cruise is a concrete, stressful problem; coordinating alternatives under timing and budget constraints provides credible value.
impact_evidence: Specific Lima-to-Miami recovery scenario with hotel and shuttle.
Multi-domain coordination and running trip cost are visible/claimed.
Explicit human confirmation for consequential bookings.
creativity_rationale: The multi-step recovery interaction is a fresh, ambitious use of a browser-native agent surface, especially without a custom conversational agent.
creativity_evidence: One agent coordinates flights, hotel, ground transport, contact notification, and itinerary.
Natural-language constraints drive stateful recovery.
No custom agent built; uses ChatGPT browser discovery directly.
usability_note: The multi-step travel state and cost summary are understandable; the shown example is over budget, which is a useful honest state.
red_flags: No submitted video; frame sheets show a repeated coding/agent workspace and do not make all travel tool calls legible.
Displayed example exceeds the stated budget, though that may be intentional constraint feedback.
standouts: Uses the browser's own agent discovery rather than a bespoke agent.
advance_reason: Strong practical impact and meaningful WebMCP-centered orchestration.

one_line: Extension that lets agents safely personalize arbitrary webpages with reversible structured plans.
what_it_does: Inspects page targets, applies atomic style/layout/interface modifications, supports rollback and persistent preferences, and avoids arbitrary JS/HTML/CSS execution.
leverage_rationale: Opaque short-lived target IDs, fingerprints, revalidation, atomic plans, and rollback provide a safer structured control surface for arbitrary webpages than generic browser automation.
leverage_evidence: About text specifies inspect_page and apply_page_plan with target freshness and atomic validation.
Claims confirmation, cancellation, rollback, persistent modifications, and dynamic shortcuts.
Frame sheet shows browser content beside an OpenCode/agent workspace, though specific calls are not legible.
execution_rationale: The concept and safety architecture are coherent, and packaging shows browser personalization/automation context, but the supplied frames mostly show repeated static media pages with little directly readable product outcome.
execution_evidence: Public repo and live demo reported alive.
Devpost packaging shows browser-controlled page and agent workspace.
No video and no clearly visible applied personalization result cap evidence.
impact_rationale: People with different accessibility needs, preferences, and workflows can benefit from local, reversible personalization on sites they do not own.
impact_evidence: Supports hide/move/style changes, shortcuts, and remembered preferences.
Works on third-party websites and keeps changes local/reversible.
Addresses modern pages changing underneath automation.
creativity_rationale: A safety-oriented personalization layer for arbitrary third-party pages is a distinctive extension of WebMCP beyond single-site apps, with a thoughtful target identity model.
creativity_evidence: Opaque target IDs and one-use snapshots avoid arbitrary selectors.
Atomic plan validation and navigation/fingerprint checks.
Combines accessibility, preference, and agent-control use cases.
usability_note: Reversible local changes are user-friendly in principle; actual personalization results are not clearly visible in the frames.
red_flags: Frames show mostly a repeated video page and OpenCode panel; applied page changes are not clearly visible.
API-key model is not explicit in the packet and is marked as an assumption from the external AI fallback.
standouts: Reversible, atomic personalization rather than unrestricted scripting.
advance_reason: Meaningful agent-control problem and strong safety design, though direct product evidence is limited.
